h1: C-frame hydraulic presses — open-gap presses, 22 to 276 US tons
intro: A C-frame (gap-frame) hydraulic press is open on three sides: small dies go in and out quickly, the operator reaches the part from the front and both sides, and the press takes less floor space than an H-frame of the same force — the press for punching, blanking and forming with small dies, press-fitting and assembly. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page: the premium line, built in Turkey on a welded monoblock frame with a chrome-plated cylinder and a T-slotted table, 33 to 276 US tons — the CFS with a pressure transmitter, light barrier and two-hand control, the CFSS with the work area enclosed by guards and a light barrier, and the CFDD for deep drawing, with a die cushion of 11 to 110 US tons and an ejector that lifts the drawn part out; and the value line, built in China — the HP-C presses from 22 to 110 US tons, open on three sides for assembling and dismantling large parts. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For larger tables and tonnages, see the H-frame presses. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

hero_brand_line: The premium-line presses are built in Turkey with European components; the value-line presses are built in China — all to NovoTech's specification and sold, installed and supported in Canada by NovoTech.

faq.a: A C-frame press is open on three sides, so small dies go in and out quickly, the part is easy to reach and the press takes less floor space. The open throat deflects slightly under load, which limits the table size and the force — the premium-line C-frame range stops at 276 US tons. For deep drawing large parts, long dies or more force, an H-frame press is stiffer and takes larger tables.

All three share the welded monoblock frame, chrome-plated cylinder and T-slotted table, from 33 to 276 US tons with a 15.7″ stroke. The CFS is the simpler press with a pressure transmitter, light barrier and two-hand control. The CFSS encloses the work area with guards and a light barrier for production with smaller dies. The CFDD adds a die cushion of 11 to 110 US tons in the lower table and an ejector, for deep drawing on a C-frame.

faq.q: Single action or double action — what is a die cushion?
faq.a: A single action press has one ram. A double action (deep drawing) press adds a die cushion in the lower table — a second cylinder that holds the blank holder with its own programmed force — so a flat blank can be drawn into a deep cup, pan or housing without wrinkling. The HDD H-frame and CFDD C-frame presses have the cushion built in; it is an option on the HCFP column press.

faq.q: Can the press be built to my die?
faq.a: Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
